original_test_intent: Validate PCIe link enable/disable interoperability on the approved HGX hierarchy by proving each NVQual Test #26 cycle disables only the intended link, then restores every expected NVIDIA endpoint at required generation/width and functional health without hang, unplanned reboot, or new errors.
original_method: Pin Test #26, link-control primitive, root-port/switch/retimer/endpoint/GPU and sibling scope, consumer quiesce, disable acknowledgment and expected absence, enable/retrain/re-enumeration deadlines, iterations/timing, complete identity/function and error acceptance; preserve baselines; record each atomic cycle before the next; stop on first scope or recovery fault and recover out of band.
manual_activity: HGX owner/FAE approves the link-control primitive, hierarchy and service impact; an operator isolates the SUT, observes out-of-band state, and owns recovery if the endpoint or host does not return.
required_inputs: Pinned NVIDIA NVQual Test #26 link enable/disable package/configuration and compatible firmware/driver
Consumer quiesce, disable/enable primitive, expected disappearance, retrain/re-enumeration, generation/width, device/function deadlines
Iteration count/timing, error acceptance, persistent storage, aborts, final state, and recovery policy
safety_requirements: Dedicated non-production HGX SUT with explicit hierarchy and disruption authorization
No unsaved workload; consumers quiesced; verified BMC/console/power recovery
Validate link ownership and sibling blast radius before any control write
Stop on wrong-scope disable, failed disable/enable, missing/misbound device, late/downtrained link, driver/GPU failure, hang/reboot, new AER, thermal/power fault, tool failure, or evidence gap
No forced rescan/rebind, reset/power escalation, clearing, or automatic retry
agent_execution_scope: Validate Test #26 configuration, hierarchy, baseline, quiesce, interlocks, ledger, and recovery
Run only the approved link-control primitive
Correlate PCIe, NVIDIA, driver, OS, BMC, console, thermal, and power health
Do not infer target, broaden scope, force recovery, retry faults, or issue the DUT verdict
engineer_actions: Approve Test #26 link-control recipe, exact hierarchy/sibling scope, iterations, and service impact
Own first-fault disposition and out-of-band recovery
Review every cycle and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: It identifies link enable/disable but supplies no control primitive or hierarchy; a final lspci/nvidia-smi view cannot prove intended disable, containment, and recovery for each cycle.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use only the pinned Test #26 primitive with an atomic ledger and block cycle N+1 until N proves scoped disable, expected absence, enable, retrain, identity-complete re-enumeration, link/function state, and acceptable error deltas.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: NVQual Test #26, link enable/disable interoperability, all-items/no-hang/no-reboot Criteria, no bundle, and 5/600-minute allocation remain; missing iterations and timing are not invented.

modernized_recommendation.status: CRITICAL INTERLOCKED HGX LINK ENABLE DISABLE INTEROPERABILITY
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Model each cycle from quiesce and pre-state through scoped disable/absence, enable/retrain, identity-complete endpoint/function recovery, and health acceptance.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds control semantics, sibling containment, transaction phases, persistent evidence, first-fault inhibition, functional recovery, and out-of-band restoration.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A healthy final endpoint cannot reveal wrong-scope disruption, a missing disable, transient downtraining, identity changes, earlier driver failure, or recovered AER events.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Selecting the wrong link hierarchy can remove multiple GPUs or unrelated siblings; failed re-enable can strand endpoints or host and encourage unsafe recovery escalation.

project_override_considerations: Vendor link-control abstraction is acceptable only when it exposes the exact hierarchy and transaction phases. SBR, FLR, retrain-only, host reboot, and power cycle are not substitutes for a true disable/enable cycle unless separately approved and recorded.
expected_evidence: Exact row/variant/hash, owner-approved Test #26 manifest/configuration, and authorization
HGX/tool/firmware/driver/BMC identities plus complete link/sibling/endpoint/GPU topology
Per-cycle atomic timeline with affected identities, link transitions, full inventory, generation/width, driver/GPU readiness, and disposition
First-fault recovery or clean final topology/link/device/host state and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Test #26 Procedure, Criteria, and same-row AI review consistently target link enable/disable interoperability. Missing hierarchy and transaction acceptance are readiness under-specification, not a competing source objective.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The link-control interoperability objective is clear. Proprietary tooling, exact hierarchy, transaction semantics, isolation, evidence, and recovery are identifiable prerequisites rather than permanent review blockers.

review_improvement: Makes each enable/disable operation a scoped, identity-complete transaction and prevents a recovered final enumeration, rescan, reset, or power cycle from masquerading as link-control interoperability.
independent_technical_reasoning: Link disable removes transport rather than merely renegotiating it, so endpoint disappearance is expected only inside a precisely bounded hierarchy. Correct recovery includes stable identities, full link width/speed and driver/GPU readiness, while siblings outside scope remain unaffected. A final inventory cannot prove those temporal and containment properties. Each cycle therefore needs durable phase evidence and first-fault inhibition before another disruption can erase the original failure context.
